deep_dive_cases.raw_narrative: Permit review identified the following: The hydraulic valve actuator (C-695) presented stored pneumatic or hydraulic energy in the actuator mechanism for the planned maintenance on a pipeline valve actuator. The intended control, verified bleed-down of stored actuator pressure with mechanical lock-out of the valve position, was incorrectly applied to the wrong isolation point. Required PPE for the task was confirmed present and correctly worn. Given the job's layout, the insulation contractor stood squarely within reach of unexpected actuator movement from residual stored pressure during servicing. The general work permit paperwork was complete and had been signed off. Left unaddressed, the scenario could have resulted in a crush or impact injury from unexpected actuator movement. A wider walk-down of similar equipment on the unit was scheduled as a result. The observation was raised with the area supervisor before the crew continued. The competent person who signed the original permit was asked to clarify the intended scope. The finding was cross-checked against the applicable procedure reference. The shift log was annotated so the incoming crew would be aware of the finding. Similar conditions had reportedly been seen elsewhere on the same work front.

deep_dive_cases.raw_narrative: Pre-job check: Cargo handler was fit-up at flare knock-out drum in maintenance workshop. The original work location had been changed to avoid a live operating area during fit-up at PRO-4728 Process pressure 29 bar. The observation was carried into the next work phase because the local arrangement around PRO-4728 had changed during fit-up. At 16:05, process pressure 29 bar was recorded and work package WO-90821 remained open for the fit-up step. Entry into the vessel was possible from the work area, while the attendant stayed at the opening, ventilation remained running, and the entrant carried a live atmospheric monitor.
